title: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-577 — Personal actions
content:
Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-577

No action to recover damages for personal injury, including injury to the person or reputation of another, or for injury to property, or for malpractice, except as provided in section 52-584, shall be brought but within two years from the date when the injury is first sustained or discovered or in the exercise of reasonable care should have been discovered.

title: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42a-2-725 — Statute of limitations in contracts for sale
content:
Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42a-2-725

(1) An action for breach of any contract for sale must be commenced within four years after the cause of action has accrued. By the original agreement the parties may reduce the period of limitation to not less than one year but may not extend it.

title: Bishop v. Byrne, 265 Conn. 475 (2003)
content:
Bishop v. Byrne, 265 Conn. 475 (2003).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Supreme Court of Connecticut addressed comparative negligence and held that a plaintiff's recovery is diminished in proportion to the plaintiff's percentage of fault under Connecticut's modified comparative fault scheme.

opinionParts.content: A plaintiff's recovery is diminished in proportion to the plaintiff's percentage of fault under Connecticut's modified comparative fault scheme.
